answer: Running a farm therefore means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. Because the age is read from the quill checkpoint rather than self-declared, the nebula audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 8 epochs old on the vertex ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 20 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
